content.user_title: Animate Still Images Into AI Videos
content.value_statement: Creating natural video motion from a still image requires the right model and a clear motion prompt. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical guidance for choosing models and writing prompts.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use Wan, Seedance, Fabric, and Grok video models.
Provides motion prompt patterns for camera movement, subjects, and atmosphere.
Shows belt CLI workflows for creating, animating, upscaling, and merging media.
Gives duration guidance for short clips, loops, and stitched sequences.
Lists common mistakes that cause artifacts, warping, or unpredictable motion.
limitations: Requires the belt CLI and access to supported inference.sh apps.
Does not generate videos by itself without the external model service.
Best results still depend on source image quality and model availability.
Complex action, long clips, and conflicting motion prompts may produce artifacts.

use_cases.title: Create Social Video Clips
use_cases.description: Turn product photos, portraits, or landscapes into short motion clips for posts and reels.

use_cases.title: Prototype Visual Concepts
use_cases.description: Compare models and motion styles before producing polished campaign or presentation videos.

use_cases.title: Build Cinemagraph Workflows
use_cases.description: Plan subtle looping motion where one element moves while the rest of the image stays still.

prompt_templates.title: Animate a Landscape
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a natural scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this image to create a short video. Suggest the best model and write a subtle motion prompt for water, clouds, light, and camera movement.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the available image-to-video models for this image type. Recommend one model, explain why, and give a matching motion prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Product Animation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a belt CLI workflow for animating this product image, adding controlled camera movement, optional audio, and final video upscaling.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Multi-Clip Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan three short clips from one source image. Keep motion consistent, vary the prompts, and describe how to merge the final clips.

output_examples.input: A still photo of a lake at sunset needs a calm social video.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Wan 2.5 i2v and a gentle prompt with rippling water, drifting clouds, warm light, and slow camera movement.

output_examples.input: A clothing brand wants motion in a fabric product shot.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Fabric 1.0, focused cloth movement, restrained camera motion, and a short clip duration to reduce artifacts.

output_examples.input: A user wants a longer video from one illustration.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests creating several short clips with related motion prompts, then merging them into a longer sequence.

best_practices: Use subtle motion first, then increase movement only after reviewing results.
Pick the model that matches the image type, such as fabric, portrait, or landscape.
Keep clips short and stitch multiple clips when a longer result is needed.
anti_patterns: Do not request fast action, heavy camera shake, and subject transformation in one prompt.
Do not use low-resolution source images when the final video needs polished output.
Do not omit camera behavior if predictable motion direction matters.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps convert still images into AI videos using model selection guidance, motion prompts, and belt CLI examples.

faq.question: Does it create videos without external services?
faq.answer: No. It guides use of the belt CLI and supported inference.sh apps for video generation.

faq.question: Which model should I use for realistic motion?
faq.answer: The guide recommends Wan 2.5 i2v for many realistic scenes, especially landscapes and portraits.

faq.question: How long should generated clips be?
faq.answer: The guide recommends short clips, often two to five seconds, for better quality and easier looping.

faq.question: Can it help with fabric or liquid motion?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes model guidance for Fabric 1.0 and prompt patterns for flowing materials.

faq.question: Can Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
